page: Microsoft Azure D192ls_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dlsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 192 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 96 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and is equipped with a 480 MB L3 cache. The system is configured with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, though it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 197908.53 and a PassMark CPU score of 150927.69. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contribute to a PassMark extended instructions score of 247926.7. Memory performance is characterized by high read-only bandwidth, reaching 14747.07 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 685.05 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. In database and key-value store benchmarks, the instance achieved 265.88 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and a top-tier PassMark database operations score.

Given its high compute density and low memory-to-vCPU ratio, the D192ls_v7 is highly cost-efficient for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. It is well-suited for multi-threaded decompression tasks, static web serving, database operations, and CPU-based machine learning inference, as demonstrated by its strong prompt processing speeds across various model sizes. However, the lack of a GPU and local NVMe storage represents a tradeoff for workloads requiring local disk caching or hardware-accelerated graphics processing.
